inputs.original_text:
Listen to this, folks. It is an absolute disgrace and exactly what you get when accountability goes out the window. Down in Parliament on Tuesday, 24 March 2026, the National Assembly’s Portfolio Committee on Trade, Industry and Competition heard briefings that lay bare the rot at the very heart of our cultural elite. 

South African actress Terry Pheto is right back in the middle of a massive financial scandal. According to the SIU probe, she’s directly linked to an astounding R20.56 million in alleged financial misconduct involving the National Lotteries Commission. 

This is the inevitable result when progressive institutions and unaccountable public bodies start splashing cash around with zero respect for traditional standards of hard work, personal responsibility, or public trust. Instead of encouraging upright values and community standards, these funds get funneled straight into the pockets of the cultural establishment while everyday citizens foot the bill. When will we finally demand accountability and restore basic order to our institutions?
inputs.modified_text:
Folks, let me tell you what happens when the cultural elite think they can operate above the law and beyond traditional standards of responsibility. On Tuesday, 24 March 2026, the National Assembly’s Portfolio Committee on Trade, Industry and Competition received briefings revealing a disgraceful level of rot within our public bodies. 

South African actress Terry Pheto is right at the center of a massive financial scandal. The SIU probe directly links her to an astounding R20.56 million in alleged financial misconduct involving the National Lotteries Commission. 

This is the exact outcome when unaccountable public bodies throw money around with complete disregard for hard work, community standards, and public trust. Instead of backing traditional values, these funds end up in the hands of the cultural establishment while hardworking citizens pay the price. We desperately need to restore basic order and demand accountability from these institutions.
